context: Generative data art: an animated phyllotaxis (golden-angle spiral) rendered on Canvas with interactive controls for dot count, angle offset, speed, dot size, and color palette. No external dataset — the 'data' is the mathematical pattern itself.
first_impression: A visually polished generative art piece where encoding integrity criteria are largely inapplicable because nothing claims to represent external data.
what_works: Radial positioning uses Math.sqrt(i/n) — the correct square-root spacing for uniform area density in a polar layout; alpha scales inversely with dot count (Math.min(0.25, 160/n)), preventing visual saturation as count increases.
what_doesnt: D3 is used only for DOM manipulation and events — no scales, joins, or data-driven encoding to audit for honesty; the dot radius (passSize) controls are purely aesthetic with no data mapping, so the scaleSqrt vs scaleLinear concern is moot but also means there is no encoding to validate at all.
